I have enough to trace the full pipeline. Here's the end-to-end path for `fmt::format("{}", x)`:

## 1. Entry point — compile-time checked call

`fmt::format` (`include/fmt/format.h:4362-4366`):
```cpp
template <typename... T>
auto format(format_string<T...> fmt, T&&... args) -> std::string {
  return vformat(fmt, fmt::make_format_args(args...));
}
```
- `fmt` isn't `const char*` — its type is `format_string<T...>`, an alias for `basic_format_string<char, T...>` (`include/fmt/base.h:2902`). Its constructor runs a `constexpr` parse of the literal against `T...` so a mismatched `"{}"` with wrong arg count/type is a **compile error**, not a runtime one.

## 2. Capturing arguments into type-erased `format_args`

`fmt::make_format_args(args...)` (`include/fmt/base.h:2016-2032`) builds a `detail::format_arg_store<Context, N, ...>` (`include/fmt/base.h:1682-1719`): a small stack array of `arg_t` slots, one per argument, filled by `detail::make_arg` (`include/fmt/base.h:1620-1661`). `make_arg` inspects `T` and either stores it inline as a `detail::value<Context>` (ints, floats, bool, char, string views, pointers, C-strings — a tagged union, `include/fmt/base.h:1728`) or, for a user type, wraps it as a `custom_value` holding a pointer to the object plus a function pointer that calls `formatter<T>::format` — this is how arbitrary user-defined types get type-erased without virtual dispatch.

`format_arg_store` converts implicitly to `basic_format_args<Context>` (`include/fmt/base.h:1842`, ctor at line 1889) — this is `format_args`, the type-erased, non-owning view of the arguments (it just holds a descriptor + a pointer into the store's array, so it must not outlive the call). Only 2 lookups needed here since `format_args`/`basic_format_arg` are the real names.

## 3. Routing through `vformat` → `vformat_to` into a buffer

`format()` calls the free `vformat(string_view fmt, format_args args)`, implemented in `include/fmt/format-inl.h:1431-1437`:
```cpp
auto vformat(string_view fmt, format_args args) -> std::string {
  auto buffer = memory_buffer();
  detail::vformat_to(buffer, fmt, args);
  return to_string(buffer);
}
```
- `memory_buffer` (`include/fmt/format.h:936`) is `basic_memory_buffer<char>` (`format.h:835-909`) — a `detail::buffer<T>` with inline stack storage that grows (reallocates, doubling) on overflow. This is the "memory buffer" all output is written into before becoming a `std::string`.
- `detail::vformat_to(buffer<Char>&, ..., args, loc)` (`include/fmt/format.h:4220-4286`) is the real engine. For the exact `"{}"` case it takes a fast path (`format.h:4223-4227`): fetch `args.get(0)` and call `arg.visit(default_arg_formatter<Char>{out, args, loc})` directly, skipping the general parser. For any other format string it drives `detail::parse_format_string` over a `format_handler` whose callbacks (`on_text`, `on_arg_id`, `on_format_specs`) walk the literal, fetch each referenced `basic_format_arg`, and dispatch it through `arg.visit(arg_formatter<Char>{...})` (or `arg.format_custom(...)` for user types, `format.h:4268`).

## 4. `basic_format_arg::visit` and formatter specializations

`basic_format_arg<Context>::visit` (`include/fmt/base.h:1779-1816`) switches on the stored type tag and calls the visitor with the concrete C++ value (`int`, `double`, `string_view`, etc.), or, for `type::custom_type`, with a `handle` (`base.h:1747-1758`) whose `format()` invokes the stored function pointer — which ultimately calls **`formatter<T, Char>::format(value, ctx)`**.

The primary `formatter<T, Char, Enable>` template (`include/fmt/base.h:1140-1144`) is deleted by default — a type is only formattable if this template has been specialized for it. Built-in specializations (ints, floats, strings, chrono types, ranges, etc.) live across `base.h`, `format.h`, `chrono.h`, `ranges.h`; each specialization's `format(value, ctx)` writes formatted text via `ctx.out()`, an output iterator (`detail::write<Char>`, e.g. `format.h:3704-3714` for the custom-type path) that appends characters/bytes into the buffer through a `basic_appender<Char>`.

For plain built-ins visited via `default_arg_formatter::operator()` (`include/fmt/format.h:3718-3735`), the value is written directly with `detail::write<Char>(out, value)` — this is the low-level integer/float/string formatting code (`format.h`/`format-inl.h`), which for our `x` example handles the actual digit/character generation and appends the result to `memory_buffer` via the appender.

## 5. Buffer → `std::string`

Once all output has been appended to the `memory_buffer`, `vformat` returns `to_string(buffer)` (`include/fmt/format.h:4202-4207`):
```cpp
auto to_string(const basic_memory_buffer<Char, SIZE>& buf) -> std::basic_string<Char> {
  auto size = buf.size();
  return std::basic_string<Char>(buf.data(), size);
}
```
This does one final copy from the buffer's storage into a freshly-constructed `std::string`, which is what `fmt::format` returns to the caller.

### Summary of the call chain
```
fmt::format("{}", x)                              [format.h:4363]
  └─ fmt::make_format_args(x)                      [base.h:2016]  → format_arg_store → format_args (type-erased)
  └─ fmt::vformat(fmt, args)                        [format-inl.h:1431]
        └─ memory_buffer buffer;                    [format.h:936/835]
        └─ detail::vformat_to(buffer, fmt, args)     [format.h:4220]
              └─ arg.visit(default_arg_formatter{})  [base.h:1779] / arg_formatter for specs
                    └─ formatter<T,Char>::format(...) → ctx.out() appends into buffer
        └─ return to_string(buffer)                  [format.h:4202]  → std::string
```

## 4. `basic_format_arg::visit` and formatter specializations

`basic_format_arg<Context>::visit` (`include/fmt/base.h:1779-1816`) switches on the stored type tag and calls the visitor with the concrete C++ value (`int`, `double`, `string_view`, etc.), or, for `type::custom_type`, with a `handle` (`base.h:1747-1758`) whose `format()` invokes the stored function pointer — which ultimately calls **`formatter<T, Char>::format(value, ctx)`**.

The primary `formatter<T, Char, Enable>` template (`include/fmt/base.h:1140-1144`) is deleted by default — a type is only formattable if this template has been specialized for it. Built-in specializations (ints, floats, strings, chrono types, ranges, etc.) live across `base.h`, `format.h`, `chrono.h`, `ranges.h`; each specialization's `format(value, ctx)` writes formatted text via `ctx.out()`, an output iterator (`detail::write<Char>`, e.g. `format.h:3704-3714` for the custom-type path) that appends characters/bytes into the buffer through a `basic_appender<Char>`.

For plain built-ins visited via `default_arg_formatter::operator()` (`include/fmt/format.h:3718-3735`), the value is written directly with `detail::write<Char>(out, value)` — this is the low-level integer/float/string formatting code (`format.h`/`format-inl.h`), which for our `x` example handles the actual digit/character generation and appends the result to `memory_buffer` via the appender.

## 5. Buffer → `std::string`

Once all output has been appended to the `memory_buffer`, `vformat` returns `to_string(buffer)` (`include/fmt/format.h:4202-4207`):
```cpp
auto to_string(const basic_memory_buffer<Char, SIZE>& buf) -> std::basic_string<Char> {
  auto size = buf.size();
  return std::basic_string<Char>(buf.data(), size);
}
```
This does one final copy from the buffer's storage into a freshly-constructed `std::string`, which is what `fmt::format` returns to the caller.

### Summary of the call chain
```
fmt::format("{}", x)                              [format.h:4363]
  └─ fmt::make_format_args(x)                      [base.h:2016]  → format_arg_store → format_args (type-erased)
  └─ fmt::vformat(fmt, args)                        [format-inl.h:1431]
        └─ memory_buffer buffer;                    [format.h:936/835]
        └─ detail::vformat_to(buffer, fmt, args)     [format.h:4220]
              └─ arg.visit(default_arg_formatter{})  [base.h:1779] / arg_formatter for specs
                    └─ formatter<T,Char>::format(...) → ctx.out() appends into buffer
        └─ return to_string(buffer)                  [format.h:4202]  → std::string
```
